why: Checks 1, 2 and 4 stay within their expect lines. Check 1's cases are plain left-padding, Check 2's inputs are all already width or longer, and Check 4 is just exit code 0 with fail 0. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its FAIL condition uses a regex, `"^#{1,6}\\s+`?" + k + "\\b"`, that only matches a markdown heading starting with the function's name. The expect line says only "a section for every function", so a section headed "## The padLeft helper" or "## Function: padLeft" would meet the words but fail the check. That exact heading-form rule is stricter than the words and should be under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL. PASS also requires "its own heading with a description beneath it" and FAIL on "no describing content". That is arguably part of what a section is, but it is still a judgment the words don't strictly force. So the criterion does not hold for the whole output.
